newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sells 75 pct in Pyramids Breweries.
newsitem.headline: Egypt sells 75 pct in Pyramids Breweries.

text.p: The Egypt state said on Tuesday it sold 74.9 percent in Pyramids Breweries to six international funds in a deal that totalled 231 million pounds.
The government sold 3.37 million shares of the brewery, also known as al-Ahram Beverages, to the unidentified funds at 68.5 pounds per share, sources close to the deal said.
The state privatised about 15 percent of the company's 4.5 million shares in July. The government had planned to sell 20 percent of the firm's equity but religious opposition dampened the deal.

The deal with anchor investors excluded the land, which the buyers would hand over to the official Holding Company for Housing, Tourism and Cinema, moving the plants within five years to new industrial cities.
The buyers are also committed to inject into the brewery new investment of 221 million pounds.
Pyramids Breweries made net after-tax profits of 42.980 million pounds in the financial year 1995/6, 35.8 percent up on 31.654 million in 1994/5.
Turnover rose to 130.100 million pounds, 11.0 percent up on 117.185 million in the previous year, and profits before tax were 59.810 million, 31.7 percent up on 45.408 million.
The shares last traded on the Egyptian stock exchange at 67.20 pounds.
